intro: Reference for external integrations. Covers public and user-facing endpoints only. Admin endpoints are not documented here.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.intro: Some public endpoints need no key but are limited per IP. Endpoints marked “auth” require a key. For /fetch-link and /history the key is optional: if you send one, the request runs under your account.
auth.note: Create an API key on the API Keys page (available on Pro, Team and Enterprise plans). Any key can be revoked at any time. A wrong or revoked key returns HTTP 401 with {"error_code":"invalid_api_key"}.

rate.title: Rate limits
rate.otherValue: 60 requests/minute — per API key (without a key: per IP)
rate.fetchValue: 30 requests/minute — per API key (without a key: per IP)
rate.exceeded: Over the rate limit: HTTP 429. Wait about a minute and try again, increasing the wait between attempts (exponential backoff). Requests that send a key are counted per key, so several servers behind one IP do not share a limit.
rate.monthlyQuota: Each request that sends an API key counts as 1 call against the account's monthly quota (UTC calendar month, resets at 00:00 UTC on the 1st). When it runs out: HTTP 429 with {"error_code":"api_monthly_quota_exceeded","reset_at":"…"}. Every response to a request with a key includes the headers X-API-Quota-Limit, X-API-Quota-Remaining, X-API-Quota-Reset (Unix time). To see how many calls you have used: GET /api/v1/api-keys/usage. Downloads made through the API also count against the daily download limit.

partner.title: Partner API (for businesses integrating from their backend)
partner.intro: For businesses that call VidGrab from their own servers. Keys that look like vgp_ are issued by VidGrab; you cannot create them yourself. To get a key, contact: {{email}} or Telegram @vidgrab_support.

notes.createJob: Create a download job. Body: { url, quality }. Returns 202 with the job details.
notes.getJob: Get the status and result of a job.
notes.listJobs: List the account's jobs (across all keys), filtered by status.
notes.usage: See today's and this month's usage against your quota.
notes.addWebhook: Register a webhook (HTTPS URL) to receive job.completed and job.failed events.
notes.validateUrls: Check a list of URLs in advance, up to 100 URLs per call.
notes.platformStatus: Shows which platforms can currently be downloaded. The webhooks platform.degraded / platform.recovered are sent when the status changes.

partner.li1: Requests per minute are counted per key (default 60). Over the limit: HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.
partner.li2: Jobs per day are counted per key (default 10,000).
partner.li3: When the daily or monthly job quota runs out: HTTP 429 with {"detail":{"code":"rate_limit_exceeded" | "monthly_quota_exceeded","reset_at":"…"}}; wait until reset_at.
partner.li4: rate_limit_exceeded = out of jobs for the day; rate_limited = too many requests per minute.
partner.li5: Polling GET /jobs/{id} does not use up the job quota.

endpoints.health: Liveness + version check. Returns disk, Redis, yt-dlp version, app_version.
endpoints.apiInfo: Public API metadata: endpoints, rate limits, auth guide, error format.
endpoints.fetchLink: Download a link and wait for the result: the request stays open until it finishes (synchronous) and returns no token to poll. With an API key it runs under your account (quota and quality follow your plan); without one it runs as a guest. quality defaults to "video" (up to 1080p); allowed values: "video", "video_fast" (faster, lower quality), "video_4k" (best available), "video_<height>" (for example "video_720"), "mp3_128", "mp3_320". The actual quality is capped by the account's plan. progress_token is optional and chosen by you: send it to follow progress through GET /progress/{token} while the request is running.
endpoints.progress: Download progress for the progress_token you sent in POST /fetch-link; only meaningful while that request is still running. An unknown token (or one with no progress yet) returns status "pending". Do not use it to get the final result: the result is in the /fetch-link response.
endpoints.history: The account's download history when an API key is sent (default limit=5; supports ?limit=&offset=&platform=&status=success|failed|processing). Guests (no key) get an empty list with local_only: true, because guest history is kept only in the browser.
endpoints.archive: Personal archive. Supports ?platform=&is_starred=&collection_id=&language=&file_status=available|pinned|expired&sort=&page=1&limit=20. There is no q parameter: use GET /api/v1/archive/search to search.
endpoints.archiveSearch: Search the archive by title, author, hashtag and notes. ?q= (at least 2 characters, required) and ?limit=20.
endpoints.errorCodes: Full catalogue of structured error codes with user-safe messages.

errorFormat.title: Error format
errorFormat.intro: Every error returns the same JSON structure:
errorFormat.fullList: See the full list of error codes

errors.provider_unavailable: The platform is temporarily not responding.
errors.extractor_broken: The platform just changed and downloads are temporarily unavailable; VidGrab is working on it. Try again in 30–60 minutes.

retry.title: Retry guidance
retry.li2: Increase the wait between attempts (exponential backoff): 1s → 2s → 4s → 8s (at most 3 attempts).
retry.li3: HTTP 429 with a vidgrab_ key: wait about a minute, then try again (there is no Retry-After header).
retry.li4: HTTP 429 with the Partner API (vgp_ key): if you went over the requests-per-minute limit, a Retry-After header is present, so wait exactly that many seconds; if the daily or monthly job quota ran out, wait until reset_at, since retrying earlier still returns 429.
retry.li5: HTTP 5xx: retry with backoff; HTTP 4xx (except 429): do not retry.
retry.li6: /fetch-link is synchronous: wait for the response to that same request and do not resend it before you have a result (each send counts as one download). To show progress, set your own progress_token and poll /progress/{token}.
